# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18 (Bu-Vb Pc18)

**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting down on an upper story

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vehāsakuṭi Sikkhāpada* is the eighteenth training rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a monk who sits or lies down on a bed or bench with detachable or unfastened legs on an unplanked upper storey of an accommodation belonging to the Saṅgha commits an offense requiring expiation or confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Dhammika, Broken Buddha]. In contemporary discussions on the classification of monastic discipline, this rule is occasionally highlighted as an example of an explicitly practical or minor precept (*khuddānukhuddaka-sikkhāpada*) designed to prevent physical hazards and structural accidents within the monastic dwelling [Dhammika, Broken Buddha].
Complete parallels to this rule are preserved widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing not only in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Parivāra*, and the corresponding *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 114), but also in the Vinayas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Mahīśāsaka, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Machine analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 461 matching passages across 83 Pali texts, demonstrating dense phraseological connections with adjacent *Pācittiya* rules (notably Pācittiya 15, 16, and 17) as well as the *Khandhaka* collections, including the *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18) and *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya*, Carmavastu, and Tibetan commentaries such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule and its full *Vibhaṅga* analysis has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
